title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Son
summary: A boy must keep his father's lighthouse running alone during a stormy night after his father is hurt on the stairs.
poll: A kid can handle a grown-up's job in an emergency if someone has taught them well.

versions.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Son
versions.text:
Yusuf lives at a lighthouse. It is by the sea. His father is the keeper. The keeper makes the light shine.

Every day, Yusuf helps his father. He learns about the lamp. He learns about the stairs. The stairs go up and up.

One night, a big storm comes. The wind is loud. The waves are big. Yusuf's father climbs the stairs to check the light.

His father falls! His foot hurts a lot. He cannot stand up. He cannot climb.

Yusuf must help. He must keep the light on. Ships need the light. The light keeps them safe from rocks.

Yusuf climbs the stairs alone. He is a little scared. But he knows what to do. His father taught him well.

Yusuf checks the lamp. He turns a switch. The beam spins and spins. It lights up the storm.

All night, the light shines. In the morning, the storm stops. The ships are safe. Yusuf's father is proud of his son.

One stormy night, strong winds howl around the walls, rattling the old windows. Tall waves crash against the sharp rocks far below. Worried about the ships still out on the dark sea, his father grabs his lantern and climbs the stairs to check the light.

Halfway up the dark stairway, his father's foot slips on a wet step, and he falls hard against the cold wall. His ankle twists badly, and the pain is so sharp that he cannot stand. He calls out loudly for his son.

Yusuf understands right away that he must take over, even though he has never done this fully alone before. Ships on the rough sea depend on the steady light to miss the sharp rocks near shore.

Taking a deep breath, Yusuf climbs the stairs by himself, holding the cold railing tightly. His legs feel shaky with every step, but he keeps going anyway, saying his father's calm words in his mind.

At the top, Yusuf checks the great lamp closely, just as he has practiced many times before. He flips the switch the right way, and the beam slowly begins to turn, cutting a path through the storm.

The light keeps shining through the long, noisy night, never once going dark. By morning, the storm fades into calm skies. Every ship reaches the harbor safely, and his father looks at his son with quiet pride.

By early morning, the ferocious storm finally dissolves gradually into calm, gray skies stretching serenely over a quiet, settling sea, and every ship out on the water reaches harbor safely, while his father, leaning gratefully on a borrowed cane beside his determined son, regards him with profound, unmistakable pride shining steadily in his tired, grateful eyes.

Because of this steady, patient teaching, Yusuf could take over his father's responsibility when it truly mattered.

HIGH.prompt: The poll states that a child can handle an adult's job in an emergency if someone has taught them well. Do you agree or disagree? Support your argument with evidence from the story about Yusuf's training and his actions during the storm.
checklist: I stated a clear position on the poll statement.
I supported my position with specific evidence from the story.
I addressed at least one point someone might make against my view.
HIGH.modelAnswer: I agree that a well-taught child can handle an adult's job in an emergency. Yusuf had spent many months learning how the lamp worked and memorizing the winding stairs, so when his father was hurt, he was not starting from nothing. His instinct to repeat his father's calm instructions, rather than panic, shows how deeply the training had sunk in. Someone might argue that a child's fear could still cause mistakes under real pressure, but the story shows Yusuf's legs shaking with fear even as he kept climbing and completed the job correctly, which suggests that solid preparation can carry a person through fear rather than being erased by it.
